title: Effect of a Nutritional and Culinary Support Intervention on Food-Related Quality of Life During Chemotherapy.
abstract: Chemotherapy adversely affects nutritional status and the eating experience in patients with cancer, yet its impact on food-related quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. The CANUT guide was developed to provide practical nutritional, sensory, and culinary support during treatment. This study aims to evaluate the effect of the CANUT intervention on food-related QoL in patients undergoing chemotherapy. Secondary objectives included health-related QoL, dietary intake, and anthropometric and functional parameters. In this RCT, 209 patients with cancer receiving chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to an intervention group (dietary counselling supported by the CANUT guide) or control group (standard care). Food-related QoL was assessed using the ALT-QVA score, reflecting chemotherapy-related sensory alterations, meal experience, digestive discomfort, and adaptive dietary behaviours. Health-related QoL (EORTC QLQ-C30), dietary intake (24-hour recall), anthropometry, and handgrip strength were collected. Outcomes were measured at baseline and after four chemotherapy cycles. Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models. Food-related QoL declined over time (-2.85±0.53, P75% of patients below recommendations at both time points. Anthropometric and functional parameters remained unchanged. The CANUT intervention did not improve food-related QoL or nutritional outcomes in a population mostly consisting of women with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy. This highlights the need for more integrated, comprehensive, and multimodal strategies addressing sensory alterations and individual characteristics of patients during chemotherapy (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05027490).

title: Suppression of Tau-tubulin kinase 1 mitigates tau phosphorylation, and Aβ mediated neurotoxicity via altered kinase network.
abstract: Tau-tubulin kinase-1 (TTBK1) is a neuron-specific serine/threonine tau kinase that is highly expressed in the entorhinal and hippocampal regions and phosphorylates microtubule-associated protein tau at sites relevant to Alzheimer's disease (AD), thereby contributing to early tau pathology. Targeting TTBK1 can be a promising therapeutic approach for AD, although how suppression of TTBK1 may change neuronal functions is poorly understood. Here we show the proteome and phosphoproteome analysis of murine primary cortical neurons transduced with adeno-associated virus (AAV) expressing short hairpin RNA (shRNA) targeting murine Ttbk1, using tandem mass tag and data independent acquisition liquid chromatography/mass-spectrometry. Suppression of TTBK1 expression by shRNA transduction increases expression of neuronal intermediate filament proteins and V1-domain subunits of the vacuolar H+-ATPase, suggesting the regulatory roles of TTBK1 on cytoskeletal dynamics and lysosomal activity. Silencing of Ttbk1 significantly reduces phosphorylation of TTBK1 and MAP1A as well as increases phosphorylation of neuronal intermediate filament proteins, indicating the regulation of microtubule-related proteins and axonal stabilization. Phosphosite-specific signature analysis identifies the kinases regulated by TTBK1 including AD-related cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (CDK5) and AKT1. Silencing of Ttbk1 significantly reduces CDK5 activator p25/p35 ratio and pT231 phospho-tau level, consistent with the reduced activity of CDK5. Finally, silencing of Ttbk1 reduces amyloid-β-induced neurotoxicity in vitro. These results suggest a close functional relationship or coordinated regulation among TTBK1 and other kinases in maintaining axonal homeostasis via phosphorylation of microtubule-associated proteins, and mediating amyloid-β toxicity, thus emphasize TTBK1 as an emerging therapeutic target of AD.

title: Thalamocortical dysconnectivity shapes cortical hierarchy disruption across illness durations in schizophrenia.
abstract: Schizophrenia is increasingly conceptualized as a disorder of circuit-level dysfunction. However, how thalamocortical abnormalities differ across cohorts with varying illness durations and relate to large-scale cortical hierarchical organization remains unclear. We analyzed resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,223 patients with schizophrenia and 1,224 matched healthy controls across 12 datasets. The datasets were grouped as early-, middle-, and late-stage cohorts. Connectivity gradient mapping was applied to characterize thalamocortical organization, and computational modeling evaluated simulated hierarchical changes after modifying thalamic-salience connectivity. We identified a schizophrenia-relevant sensorimotor-salience-association axis that captures systematic differences in thalamocortical abnormality profiles across the stage cohorts. Along this axis, case-control effects in association regions were positive in the early-stage cohort but negative in the middle- and late-stage cohorts, whereas sensorimotor regions showed the converse pattern. This cross-cohort pattern was accompanied by reduced cortical hierarchical separation in cohorts with longer illness duration. In contrast, salience-related thalamic regions showed negative case-control effects in all three stage cohorts, with larger effect sizes in the middle- and late-stage cohorts, and these alterations were associated with clinical symptoms. Computational modification of thalamic-salience connectivity increased simulated cortical hierarchical differentiation, particularly in the middle-stage cohort. These findings indicate that thalamocortical dysconnectivity, centered on disrupted thalamic-salience interactions, is associated with systematic differences in cortical hierarchical organization across cohorts. The cross-cohort pattern of salience-related abnormalities highlights thalamic-salience coupling as a circuit-level link to cortical hierarchical differentiation and a candidate for future mechanistic and interventional investigation.

title: Brain NaV1.5 fine-tunes neuronal excitability to facilitate female-directed social behavior in male mice.
abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5, an essential subtype for cardiac action potential generation, is also enriched in limbic regions of the brain, but its function in the central nervous system remains poorly understood. We performed RNAscope, immunostaining, electrophysiology, fiber photometry, Scn5a knockdown, and behavioral testing to dissect the functional role of NaV1.5 in the brain. NaV1.5 channels are enriched in neurons of posterior bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNSTp) and accumulated at the axon initial segment. Activation of these tetrodotoxin-resistant channels lowers action potential threshold and accelerates spike initiation at relatively hyperpolarized levels of membrane potential (Vm). In vivo fiber photometry showed that BNSTp NaV1.5-expressing neurons in male mice were recruited by salient social stimuli and exhibited hyperpolarizing Vm dynamics during social contacts. Scn5a knockdown selectively attenuated neuronal responses to female chemosensory cues, and disrupted sex preference and female-directed behaviors. These findings identify NaV1.5 as a Vm state-dependent regulator of BNSTp neuronal excitability, and reveal an unexpected role of this channel subtype in female-cue processing and female-directed social behavior in males.

title: Processing canonical and non-canonical word orders in Turkish: behavioral and ERP evidence from adults and children.
abstract: Turkish permits grammatical non-canonical word order while morphological case marking disambiguates thematic roles. We examined comprehension accuracy and verb-locked event-related potentials (ERPs) to Turkish canonical subject-object-verb (SOV) and non-canonical object-subject-verb (OSV) sentences in adults (n = 67; 18-44 years) and children (n = 37; 4.3-9.7 years). Accuracy was lower for OSV than SOV in both groups, with a significantly larger SOV-OSV accuracy difference in children. Adults showed a late posterior OSV > SOV positivity, with significant effects in several prespecified windows within the 600-1,200-ms interval, consistent with increased sentence-final processing demands associated with the non-canonical configuration at the final verb. Children showed no reliable corresponding positivity after correction for multiple comparisons. Critically, however, Group × Sentence Type interactions did not survive correction, providing insufficient evidence that the magnitude of the SOV-OSV ERP effect differed between adults and children. Within children, chronological age showed no reliable linear or quadratic association with the behavioral or ERP SOV-OSV difference across the sampled age range. By contrast, stronger grammatical ability predicted higher comprehension accuracy in both sentence types beyond age; the same general pattern was obtained for broader language ability. Neither grammatical nor broader language ability reliably modulated the SOV-OSV ERP difference. Overall, the findings suggest that the availability of morphosyntactic case cues does not by itself entail adult-like efficiency in integrating those cues during sentence comprehension, and that developmental patterns may be expressed differently across behavioral and electrophysiological measures.

title: From trauma capacity to neurotrauma capacity: A scoping review of existing assessment frameworks.
abstract: Neurotrauma, comprising traumatic brain injury (TBI) and traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI), remains a major global health issue, with low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) bearing a disproportionate burden. Effective neurotrauma care requires timely and coordinated access to prehospital care, imaging, surgery, neurocritical care, and rehabilitation, yet current assessment frameworks often fail to capture these interdependent requirements. What instruments are currently available to evaluate trauma and neurosurgical capacity across diverse global settings, and to what extent do these tools capture indicators relevant to neurotrauma care? We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Global Health from inception to March 2026, supplemented by grey literature. We included studies describing instruments assessing system or facility-level capacity for trauma or neurosurgical care. Data extraction and domain mapping were performed independently by two reviewers. Twenty-six documents were included, describing 19 distinct instruments. Instruments were categorized as surgical capacity (n = 4), trauma capacity (n = 4), neurosurgical/neurocritical care capacity (n = 4), and quality indicator sets (n = 7). Emergency and imaging readiness was the most frequently covered domain (89%), followed by quality and audit systems (68%), operative capacity (53%), and neurocritical care (47%). Prehospital referral systems and workforce/training were the least covered domains (37% each). Only two instruments covered all six predefined neurotrauma domains. Existing tools assess important components of trauma and neurosurgical capacity but remain heterogeneous and fragmented. No identified instrument provides a comprehensive, multidisciplinary assessment of neurotrauma capacity across the full continuum of care. These findings support the development of an integrated framework combining indicators across the neurotrauma care pathway.

title: Reward positivity and affective functioning in early childhood: evidence from temporospatial principal components analysis.
abstract: Reward-related Positivity (RewP) indexes neural sensitivity to reward feedback and has been widely studied in adolescents and adults. However, little is known about how individual differences in RewP are associated with emotional functioning during early childhood, a critical period for affective development. Interpretation of feedback-related ERPs in children is further complicated by temporally overlapping components. This study examined whether a principal component analysis (PCA)-derived RewP is associated with affective functioning in children aged 4-7 years. Electroencephalography was recorded from 140 children during an age-appropriate reward task. Temporospatial PCA was performed on the full EEG sample (n = 140), and primary regression analyses were conducted in the subset with complete covariate data (n = 48). Temporospatial PCA was applied to isolate a RewP component differentiating gain from loss feedback. Positive and negative affect were assessed using the child version of the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule. Regression analyses examined whether PCA-derived RewP- and gain-related P200 amplitudes were associated with affective functioning while controlling for age, sex, ethnicity, income-to-need ratio, child depressive symptoms, and parental depressive symptoms. At the group level, boys showed greater PCA-derived gain-related P200 amplitudes than girls. At the individual level, higher child positive affect was associated with larger PCA-derived RewP amplitudes in the primary covariate-adjusted regression model. In sensitivity analyses conducted in the larger sample without the income-to-needs covariate, negative affect, rather than positive affect, was significantly associated with PCA-derived RewP amplitude. These findings provide novel evidence that RewP may serve as an early neural marker of affective functioning. By extending RewP research to an understudied developmental period and emphasizing normative emotional functioning, this study advances understanding of early reward processing and highlights the utility of PCA for isolating meaningful ERP components in children.

title: Whole genome sequencing identifies genetic variants associated with senescence-accelerated phenotype of OXYS rats.
abstract: Age is the primary risk factor for age-related diseases, the early onset of which manifests as premature aging, whereas delayed development forms the basis for healthy aging and longevity. Adverse genetic variants contribute to premature aging and its diverse manifestations, including increased multimorbidity. Identifying the genetic underpinnings of premature aging and developing preventive approaches are essential to extending the human healthspan, which requires fundamental research using animal models. In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing (coverage depth >25×) of OXYS rats - a unique model of premature aging characterized by the early onset of geriatric disorders, including cataracts, AMD-like retinopathy, Alzheimer's disease-like pathology, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy - using the parental Wistar/Icgn rat strain as a control. The screening for single-nucleotide variants (SNVs), short insertions/deletions (indels), and copy number variations (CNVs) and comparative genomic analysis revealed genetic variants unique to OXYS rats that are absent in other rat strains. Specifically, we identified a large deletion in the Fat1 enhancer, deletions in the promoter regions of Abcf1 and Gsta6, and missense variants in Cic, Akap6, Nqo2, Cerkl, Bfsp1, and Cmya5 that lead to amino acid substitutions in highly conserved protein regions. Bioinformatic analysis suggested that these variants may contribute to the key features of premature aging in OXYS rats. Notably, deletions in the Fat1 enhancer and Gsta6 promoter, alongside missense substitutions in Cic, Akap6, and Nqo2, may drive early neurodegeneration and cognitive deficits by disrupting neurogenesis, reducing neuronal survival, and impairing antioxidant defense. The deletion in the Abcf1 promoter and the missense variants in Cerkl may induce retinopathy features by disrupting retinal homeostasis and weakening the protection of photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells against oxidative stress and apoptosis. Furthermore, the missense substitution in Bfsp1 likely contributes to early cataract development by reducing the stability of lens intermediate filaments. Finally, missense variants in Cmya5 and Akap6 may promote sarcopenia and cardiomyopathy via the destabilization of myofibrils in skeletal muscles and cardiomyocytes (Cmya5) and through impaired skeletal muscle regeneration and structural disorganization of cardiomyocytes (Akap6).

title: Sleep disturbances promote colorectal cancer perineural invasion via GABA-mediated BDNF secretion.
abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a hallmark of aggressive colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, often leading to poor patient outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests a link between sleep disturbances and cancer progression through neural pathways. In this study, we investigated how sleep disturbances contribute to PNI in CRC via γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Clinical data revealed that CRC patients with poor sleep quality exhibited higher PNI rates and worse prognoses. Sleep-deprived mice showed increased CNS-derived GABA levels and compromised blood-brain barrier integrity, facilitating peripheral GABA exposure. GABA treatment enhanced CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion by upregulating FOS expression, which in turn increased BDNF secretion. Elevated BDNF activated Schwann cells through the TrkB receptor, promoting their proliferation, migration, invasion, and angiogenesis. Knockdown of FOS or inhibition of TrkB mitigated these effects. Additionally, GABA was found to promote FOS transcription via upregulation of EGR1. Our findings unveil a novel mechanism whereby sleep disturbances exacerbate CRC progression through the GABA-EGR1-FOS-BDNF axis, highlighting the importance of sleep quality in CRC management and suggesting potential therapeutic targets to inhibit PNI.

title: Targeting the Parkinson's disease interactome: a systems pharmacology and molecular dynamics investigation unveils Berberis aristata-derived phytoconstituents as potential modulators of tyrosine hydroxylase and p53: a systems and molecular dynamics investigation.
abstract: Parkinson disease (PD) is a heterogeneous disorder of complex etiology involving the loss of motor activities. These findings included mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation of the brain; the deposition of certain proteins within dopaminergic neurons. Berberis aristata DC, a plant traditionally used as anti-diabetic herb in Ayurvedic system of medicine. It has also been found to have neuro-protective properties. We first screened a broad range of the photochemical and then used network pharmacology to calculate association between the target proteins and proteome components. The map of protein-protein interactions produced a large overlap between plant targets and the known PD biomarkers; and the hub proteins, TP53, tyrosine hydroxylase, DRD2, MAOB, and CASP3 were highly central and showed central function in the pathophysiology of PD. Molecular docking demonstrated high binding affinities, especially between the compound meratin and the DNA-binding area of the TP53, and quercetin and the catalytic site of tyrosine hydroxylase. Integrated systems bioinformatics workflow was implemented. The stability of these complexes at long time was verified by molecular dynamics simulations at 100 ns. The functional enrichment analysis identified participation in dopaminergic synaptic signaling, apoptotic mechanisms, and neurotrophin-mediated mechanisms. Predictions of pharmacokinetics showed that key alkaloid constituents were able to traverse through the blood-brain barrier and displayed a low toxicity level. Comprehensively, these results underpin the traditional use of Berberis aristata DC, suggesting its potential to modulate dopamine transmission and apoptotic repression, and making it a good candidate in multi-target Parkinson disease treatments.

title: Transcriptomic insights into loperamide-induced gastric dysmotility: RNA-seq analysis of a mouse model.
abstract: Loperamide, a μ-opioid receptor agonist that slows gastrointestinal transit, is widely used as an antidiarrheal agent and an experimental model of gastric dysmotility and functional dyspepsia (FD). However, transcriptomic alterations associated with loperamide-induced delayed gastric emptying remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate gastric gene-expression profiles associated with loperamide-induced gastric dysmotility using RNA sequencing. Male BALB/c mice were intraperitoneally injected with loperamide after 20 h of fasting. Delayed gastric emptying was assessed in one cohort, while gastric antrum tissues from a separate cohort were collected for RNA sequencing. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using fold change ≥1.5 and false discovery rate (FDR) <0.01. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and pathway-network analysis were conducted to characterize biological pathways associated with loperamide treatment. Loperamide significantly delayed gastric emptying, as demonstrated by increased gastric retention of phenol red. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,356 DEGs, including 553 upregulated and 803 downregulated genes. GSEA revealed enrichment of inflammatory response-related pathways among upregulated genes, whereas synaptic transmission- and calcium signaling-related pathways were predominantly downregulated. Representative genes involved in cholinergic signaling (Chrm2 and Chrna9), glutamatergic signaling (Grm7), and calcium-channel function (Cacna1a) showed reduced expression, while Il33 was increased. This study provides transcriptomic insights into loperamide-induced gastric dysmotility. The findings suggest coordinated downregulation of genes associated with neuronal/synaptic signaling together with enrichment of inflammatory response-related transcriptional pathways in the gastric antrum, providing a molecular framework for this widely used experimental model.

title: Simultaneous hyperkinetic movement disorders phenotyping: a cross-cohort pediatric transfer study using routine videos, markerless pose estimation and a tabular foundation model.
abstract: Accurate recognition of movement disorders (MDs) phenomenology remains a demanding task in pediatric practice, compounded by mixed and evolving motor presentations, inter-examiner expertise variability, and the scarcity of structured digital tools validated across age groups. A child with combined MDs may receive different phenomenological diagnoses from different examiners, with direct consequences for etiological guidance, treatment planning, neuromodulation candidacy, and longitudinal monitoring. Video-based examination is already central to expert practice, but its systematic analysis remains frequently inaccessible because of limited human resources. To develop and externally test a video-based framework for simultaneous detection of hyperkinetic MDs phenomenologies: dystonia, tremor, myoclonus, chorea, athetosis, ballismus, stereotypies, and tics using routine clinical recordings, with external, cross-cohort transfer from adult to pediatric populations. In this proof-of-concept study, the framework combines markerless pose estimation, kinematic descriptors, and a pretrained foundation model. A shared predictive backbone was developed on 21 adults with confirmed hyperkinetic MDs and 4 healthy controls. External validation was performed on an independent cohort: a real-world pediatric sample (n = 12, monogenic combined MDs). For the external dataset, the backbone was deployed without retraining; lightweight calibration adjusted only the final subject-level decision step using a clinician-labeled small representative subset of patients. After local calibration of the decision layer on the clinician-selected subset, performance improved on the held-out pediatric patients (n = 7): Hamming accuracy rose from 0.804 to 0.839 and the Jaccard index from 0.548 to 0.633 (true positives 8 to 13, false negatives 9 to 4, false positives 2 to 5, across 56 patient-phenomenology decisions). Given the small held-out sample, these estimates should be regarded as exploratory. This calibrated performance was preserved, and the Jaccard index further improved, when the evaluation was restricted to the phenomenologies with more definite clinician agreement (Hamming accuracy 0.9, Jaccard index 0.786), indicating that the gains did not rest on the least-reliable labels. A two-stage strategy, a reusable predictive backbone combined with lightweight, site-specific adaptation, may offer a practical and scalable route to routine-video-based digital phenotyping of MDs across age groups. A shared backbone trained on standardized adult recordings transferred phenotyping signal to an independent, real-world pediatric cohort without retraining. Local calibration of the decision layer improved performance in this small exploratory cohort, while clinical-grade reliability across the full phenotypic spectrum remains to be confirmed in larger cohorts.

title: Linking liver fibrosis to cardiac structure, function, and heart disease: a community-based fibrosis-4 index study.
abstract: The Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) is a non-invasive tool used to assess advanced liver fibrosis. Although liver fibrosis has been linked to heart disease, its relationship with cardiac structure and function remains unclear. This study examined associations of FIB-4 with incident heart disease and cardiac morpho-functional phenotypes and explored whether cardiac phenotypes statistically accounted for part of the association. In this prospective cohort study using the UK Biobank, 416,001 participants without known heart or liver disease at baseline (mean age 56.15 ± 8.09 years; 55.78% female) were followed for up to 17 years. FIB-4, calculated from age, AST, ALT, and platelet count, was analyzed continuously and using a high-risk threshold of >2.67. Incident coronary heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias (CA), and heart failure (HF) were identified from linked records. A subset of 33,927 participants underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging a median of 10.20 years after baseline. Over a median follow-up of 14.61 years, 57,207 participants (13.75%) developed heart disease. Higher FIB-4 was associated with CA (HR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.24-1.41), HF (HR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.14-1.47), greater LV mass (β=0.014, 95% CI 0.0003-0.027), chamber dilation, reduced atrial ejection fractions, and LV remodeling. Exploratory pathway analysis indicated that LA ejection fraction statistically accounted for 36.38% of the FIB-4-CA/HF association; causal mediation cannot be inferred. Elevated FIB-4 was associated with incident CA and HF and with adverse CMR phenotypes. Exploratory pathway results were consistent with indirect pathways through cardiac remodeling, but the observational design and single CMR assessment preclude causal or temporal interpretation. FIB-4 may help identify people at higher cardiovascular risk.

title: Breast cancer brain metastasis: mechanisms, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM) is a clinically distinct form of metastatic breast cancer that causes substantial neurological morbidity and mortality. This review examines the biological bottlenecks that precede a detectable brain lesion: survival in the circulation, interaction with the cerebral endothelium, passage across the blood-brain barrier (BBB), persistence in neural tissue, and intracranial outgrowth. We emphasize how astrocytes, microglia, neurons, stromal cells, and the nutrient environment of the brain shape these events and influence treatment response. These biological features also shape disease assessment. Magnetic resonance imaging defines lesion burden but cannot reliably determine molecular status, whereas tissue sampling is invasive and plasma biomarkers may underrepresent disease confined to the central nervous system. We therefore examine the complementary roles and current limitations of tissue reassessment, blood- and cerebrospinal fluid-based liquid biopsy, molecular imaging, and artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis. Experimental evidence is interpreted according to the questions that individual models can answer. Spontaneous, intravascular, and intracranial models retain different stages of the metastatic cascade, while immunocompetent, patient-derived xenograft, and organoid systems differ in their ability to reproduce immune interactions and patient heterogeneity. Treatment is considered by subtype and clinical setting, including the need for immediate local control, intracranial disease burden, leptomeningeal involvement, previous therapy, and extracranial disease status. Clinical evidence is most developed for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive BCBM, whereas treatment of hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative disease and triple-negative breast cancer remains more dependent on local therapy and systemic indications derived from extracranial disease. Linking brain-specific mechanisms with biomarker selection, model interpretation, and subtype-guided treatment may improve the translation of experimental findings into clinically meaningful strategies.

title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of an integrative psychotherapy incorporating an attachment-based approach for adolescents with cannabis use disorder (TIMCA).
abstract: Cannabis is the most used illicit substance among adolescents. Regular cannabis use is linked to cognitive and psychosocial difficulties. As no pharmacological treatment has proven effective, psychological interventions, including motivational interviewing (MI), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family-based approaches, remain central. However, adolescent-specific evidence remains limited. TIMCA was developed as a ten-session integrative psychotherapy combining MI, CBT, and integrated attachment therapy. While family therapy may not be indicated for all adolescents, parental involvement remains important for the adolescent-parent relationship. TIMCA therefore combines individual and parent-adolescent sessions to address cannabis use alongside attachment-related and emotion-regulation processes. This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of TIMCA and explored changes over time in cannabis use and relational, emotional, anxiety/depressive, and treatment-adherence outcomes compared with treatment as usual (TAU). Thirty-nine adolescents with cannabis use disorder were randomly assigned to TIMCA (n = 19) or TAU (n = 20) in two outpatient addiction services in the Paris metropolitan area. Cannabis use, attachment security, emotion regulation, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 1-month follow-up using self-report measures and urine toxicology. TIMCA was feasible and acceptable, with high treatment adherence. Exploratory analyses showed significant within-group changes, including reductions in cannabis use, emotion dysregulation, and depressive symptoms, along with improved attachment security. In TAU, within-group changes did not reach statistical significance, and no significant between-group differences were detected. TIMCA appears feasible and acceptable, supporting further evaluation in adequately powered trials with longer follow-up.

title: AI-driven CT assessment of erector spinae myosteatosis: muscle quality and its association with strength and frailty in older surgical patients.
abstract: Frailty and sarcopenia are overlapping syndromes that increase adverse outcomes in older adults. Computed tomography (CT) is a reference standard for body composition analysis, but manual segmentation is time-consuming. This exploratory study used a fully automated deep learning model (DLM) to investigate associations between CT-derived muscle quality and quantity and clinical frailty. We performed a retrospective, cross-sectional secondary analysis of 53 geriatric surgical patients (mean age 77.4 ± 4.4 years). A DLM segmented skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue at the third lumbar vertebral level. Intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) was quantified exclusively within the erector spinae muscle and is therefore reported as a surrogate marker of trunk muscle quality rather than whole-muscle myosteatosis. Frailty was assessed with the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), handgrip strength and the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test. Because functional testing was incomplete, effective sample sizes varied (n = 21-53) and are reported for every model. In the total cohort, a higher IMAT Index was associated with lower handgrip strength (ρ = -0.434, p = 0.004, n = 43) and remained independent after adjustment for age, sex, BMI and ASA status (B = -1.808, 95% CI -2.994 to -0.622, p = 0.004, n = 42). Its association with the CFS was borderline univariately (ρ = 0.273, p = 0.051, n = 52) and absent after adjustment (p = 0.184, n = 51). Neither index was independently associated with TUG performance (p = 0.134 and p = 0.071, n = 25). In an exploratory sex-stratified analysis, the IMAT Index correlated with the CFS in women (ρ = 0.727, p < 0.001, n = 19) but not in men. Because the female subgroup was small (n = 20), no sex-stratified regression or interaction test was performed. In this small, retrospective, cross-sectional cohort, an erector-spinae-based IMAT Index was associated with handgrip strength but not independently with global clinical frailty. Automated opportunistic CT analysis may therefore identify specific muscle weakness rather than global frailty. The observed sex differences are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered longitudinal studies.

title: Transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the right globus pallidus interna in schizophrenia: A randomized, sham-controlled pilot study.
abstract: Functional abnormalities of the globus pallidus interna (GPi) are linked to psychosis severity and treatment response in schizophrenia. Transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a noninvasive method for precisely targeting deep brain structures. The effects of GPi-targeted TUS on psychosis had not been examined. We conducted a random-order, sham-controlled, crossover pilot study assessing safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of right GPi TUS for psychotic symptoms. Ten outpatients (mean age 37.5; 50% female) with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder and persistent psychosis received one TUS and one sham session, one week apart. TUS was MRI-guided, targeting right GPi with a 350 kHz transducer (100 Hz pulse repetition frequency, 5% duty cycle, in situ I spta 400 mW/cm²). Outcomes-delusion experience sampling assessment (DESA) and auditory hallucinations rating scale (AHRS)-were measured before, during, and immediately, 1 h, 1, and 7 days after stimulation. DESA scores decreased significantly more after TUS than sham (p = 0.002, Cohen's d = 0.68); AHRS and cognition changes were not significant. Mild transient adverse effects occurred in both conditions; none were serious. GPi-targeted TUS was safe, well-tolerated, and associated with a preliminary reduction in delusional severity, warranting further study in larger, randomized trials. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05643196, registered 21 November 2022.

title: Beyond pharmacology: The mediating role of expectations in the experience of side effects in anxious patients treated with secukinumab.
abstract: Biologics such as the interleukin-17A inhibitor secukinumab have significantly advanced the treatment of psoriasis. However, when discussing treatments, the role of expectations in the perception of side effects is not yet entirely clear. It is known, however, that negative expectations can cause nocebo effects. We investigated whether side-effect expectations mediate the relationship between trait anxiety and the reporting of side effects during secukinumab therapy. This post-hoc analysis used data from a randomized controlled trial in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. At the start of the study, trait anxiety and expectations regarding side effects were assessed; self-reported side effects were recorded at weeks 4 and 16. The side-effect outcomes were square-root-transformed prior to analysis to address distributional skew. All mediation steps were estimated using linear regression. Data from N = 104 participants were analyzed. Higher trait anxiety was associated with more self-reported side effects at week 4, but not at week 16. The association at week 4 was mediated by expectations regarding side effects assessed at baseline. The results indicate a nocebo effect in more anxious patients in the first weeks of treatment, with anxiety linked to negative treatment expectations which in turn were associated with the experience of side effects. Over time, the level of experienced side effects decreased significantly, potentially due to positive learning experiences occurring over the course of the treatment. Our findings emphasize the significance of targeted patient-centred communication to optimize treatment adherence.

title: 5-HT2A receptor activation induces CB1-dependent presynaptic inhibitory long-term depression in the nucleus accumbens core.
abstract: The serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2A) is a Gq/11-coupled receptor implicated in reward processing, neuropsychiatric disorders, and the actions of serotonergic psychedelics. Although 5-HT2A activation has been shown to engage endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling in several brain regions, its role in inhibitory synaptic plasticity within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether 5-HT2A activation modulates GABAergic synaptic transmission onto medium spiny neurons (MSNs) in the mouse NAc core. Using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, we found that activation of 5-HT2A receptors with the selective agonist TCB-2 induced a robust inhibitory long-term depression (iLTD) of evoked GABAergic synaptic transmission. This depression was accompanied by reduced spontaneous and miniature IPSC frequency, increased paired-pulse ratio, and changes in coefficient of variation analysis consistent with a presynaptic reduction in GABA release probability. Mechanistically, iLTD was occluded by the CB1 receptor agonist WIN55,212-2 and blocked by the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251, supporting a critical role for endocannabinoid signaling. Furthermore, iLTD induction required postsynaptic G-protein signaling, phospholipase Cβ (PLCβ) activity, and synthesis of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG). Together, these findings demonstrate that 5-HT2A activation induces a CB1-dependent presynaptic iLTD through a postsynaptic PLCβ/2-AG signaling cascade. These results demonstrate that 5-HT2A receptor activation engages endocannabinoid signaling to regulate inhibitory synaptic transmission in the NAc, highlighting a mechanism through which 5-HT2A signaling may modulate mesolimbic circuit function.

title: The association between older adult abuse and emergency department attendance and mental health service use.
abstract: Older adult abuse is associated with a higher risk of mental health disorders but to date older adult abuse has not been investigated as a predictor of mental healthcare outcomes. The purpose of this study was to systematically ascertain recorded abuse and analyse its consequences in older people receiving mental healthcare. In a large South London mental healthcare data platform, recorded older adult abuse was ascertained using natural language processing algorithms during the first 3 months of contact and investigated in relation to risk of subsequent emergency department attendance and 12-month mental health service contacts. Analyses were stratified by gender, ethnicity, marital status, and deprivation. Of 14,591 patients seen by mental health services, 8.4% were recorded as having experienced some form of abuse. Physical abuse was the most common type and financial abuse the least common. In adjusted models, only emotional abuse was associated with emergency department attendance (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.13, 95% CI: 1.02-1.26), but all abuse subtypes were associated with higher mental health service contact, most strongly for recorded sexual abuse (adjusted incidence rate ratio: 2.35, 95% CI: 1.93-2.86). Abuse experiences are commonly recorded in older adults receiving mental healthcare and are associated with a higher level of mental health service contact. With the use of natural language processing, we were able to successfully gain a deeper insight into the outcomes of abuse experienced by adults referred to a range of services.

title: Chronic post-traumatic stress disorder-related behavioral traits develop in female rats exposed to repetitive low-level blast injury and are reversible with (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine.
abstract: Many military Veterans who experienced blast-related injuries during military service suffer from chronic cognitive and mental health problems. Women constitute more than 15% of active-duty U. S. military personnel and are the fastest-growing population of U. S. Veterans. For more than a decade, we have studied a rat model of repetitive low-level blast exposure designed to mimic the type of blast-related exposure that is common in military settings. Male rats develop chronic cognitive and post-traumatic stress disorder-related traits that appear in a delayed fashion and persist for more than 1 year after exposure. These traits can be reversed with a single dose of (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine [(2R,6R)-HNK]. This study aimed to determine whether female rats develop a similar set of neurobehavioral alterations. Ten-week-old female rats were exposed to 75.1 kPa blast overpressures delivered once per day for three consecutive days. We tested female rats behaviorally between 1 and 4 weeks after blast exposure and again at 28 and 29 weeks. Rats were tested in an elevated zero maze, light-dark emergence task, and novel object recognition task, as well as contextual and cued fear learning and a Barnes maze. We tested how females would respond to a single dose of 20 mg/kg (2R,6R)-HNK administered intraperitoneally. Following blast exposure, female rats developed chronic cognitive and behavioral traits. The full behavioral phenotype developed with a delay. Treatment with a single dose of (2R,6R)-HNK reversed behavioral changes in female rats, and beneficial effects on behavior were sustained for 4 weeks without additional drug administration. As in male rats, female rats showed elevated metabotropic glutamate receptor mGluR2. Elevations of mGluR2 were reversed by (2R,6R)-HNK treatment. Similar to male rats, the serotonin receptor 5-HT2AR was decreased in blast-injured female rats but levels were not affected by (2R,6R)-HNK treatment. These studies show that female rats develop a similar behavioral profile as previously observed in male rats using the same blast exposure conditions. They further support (2R,6R)-HNK as a promising therapeutic candidate for treatment of blast-induced neurobehavioral effects, even when administered after traits are well established.

title: Complexity of plantar flexor torque and gait covaries in older adults: a network physiology approach to neuromuscular aging.
abstract: Falls are a leading cause of injury, disability, and loss of independence in older adults, and are closely linked to age-related declines in neuromuscular function. Underlying these declines is a loss of physiological complexity, reflected in more predictable and repetitive temporal structures (i.e., decreased entropy) of motor output. Within a network physiology framework, this loss of complexity may manifest as reduced network dimensionality. It may also be consistent with an increased co-variation between motor outputs in different tasks. Therefore, the present study examined the relationship between the complexity of plantar flexor torque and gait in young and older adults. Thirty-eight healthy older adults and forty-six healthy young adults participated in a single laboratory session. Plantar flexor torque and gait were assessed in separate tasks: submaximal isometric contractions and continuous treadmill walking, respectively. Complexity was inferred from sample entropy, which quantifies the temporal structure of both signals. A positive Bayesian correlation between torque and gait complexity was observed in older adults (τ = 0.245, BF10 = 3.985). In contrast, an absence of such correlation was found in young adults (τ = -0.079, BF10 = 0.257). The Bayesian comparison of the two correlations revealed a stronger association between gait and torque in older adults compared to young adults (Δτ = 0.324, BF10 = 3.456). These findings are consistent with, but do not directly demonstrate, an age-related loss of dimensionality in the neuromuscular network, in which motor outputs that vary independently in young adults co-vary in older adults. By identifying plantar-flexor torque complexity as a potential modifiable factor that is associated with gait complexity in older adults, these results motivate longitudinal work testing whether interventions that target torque control, such as resistance training, can elicit corresponding improvements in gait and thereby reduce fall risk.

title: Progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes in fresh embryo transfers: a retrospective threshold analysis of GnRH antagonist versus agonist long protocols.
abstract: Elevated progesterone levels on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) trigger are known to adversely affect pregnancy outcomes in fresh embryo transfer (fET) cycles, but their impact on neonatal outcomes remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes, and to explore the progesterone threshold, so as to provide reference for clinical decision-making. This retrospective cohort study included 2, 201 patients who achieved singleton live births following fET between April 1, 2021 and December 31, 2024. All patients were ≤ 42 years of age and underwent either a GnRH antagonist protocol or an agonist long protocol. A multivariable regression analysis was performed to detect the relationship between progesterone level and neonatal outcomes. Smooth curve fitting and threshold effect analysis were used to evaluate the cutoff value of progesterone level. In the overall population, higher progesterone levels were significantly associated with increased risks of preterm delivery (PTD) (adjusted OR: 1.89, 95% CI: 1.03 to 3.47, P = 0.0399) and low birthweight (LBW) (adjusted OR: 2.67, 95% CI: 1.14 to 6.24, P = 0.0231). These associations were observed only in the GnRH antagonist protocol, particularly with progesterone ≥ 1.0 ng/mL significantly elevating the risks of PTD (adjusted OR: 4.54, 95% CI: 2.16 to 9.56, P = 0.0021) and LBW (adjusted OR: 4.16, 95% CI: 1.15 to 15.07, P = 0.0378). Threshold analysis further identified progesterone > 0.90 ng/mL as the inflection point for PTD (adjusted OR: 6.60, 95% CI: 2.52 to 14.56, P = 0.0131) and progesterone > 0.98 ng/mL for LBW (adjusted OR: 7.50, 95% CI: 3.71 to 15.87, P = 0.0038) in antagonist cycles. No such associations were found in the GnRH agonist long protocol. Our findings suggest that in GnRH antagonist cycles, a serum progesterone level exceeding 0.90 ng/mL on hCG trigger day may serve as an independent predictor of an increased risk of PTD in singletons born after fET. These results highlight the need for enhanced perinatal surveillance in this population, and call for further validation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

title: Elevated local field potential power characterizes choreic storms identified by deep brain stimulator event capture.
abstract: Some patients with hyperkinetic movement disorders may present with a severe and prolonged state of uncontrolled chorea and/or ballism, termed 'choreic storm', causing distress and prompting intervention. These events may be more frequent and severe in patients with childhood-onset movement disorders. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) can be effective for medically refractory dyskinesias including chorea, and the availability of event-based local field potential (LFP) sensing in clinically available devices present an opportunity to better understand the underlying neurophysiology of these episodic phenomena. We analyzed clinical, electrophysiological, and corroborating video data from a patient with a de novo CEP85L mutation (NM_001042475.2, c.2381A>G, p.Y794C) presenting with chorea-predominant dyskinetic cerebral palsy, microcephaly, and intellectual disability. The patient underwent bilateral pallidal DBS for medically refractory symptoms and showed improvement in her baseline chorea. However, choreic storms continued multiple times per week, requiring frequent rescue medications and/or emergency medical intervention. These episodes were associated with autonomic features and variable triggers. Family-initiated LFP event recording supplemented by concurrent video facilitated side-by-side analysis of clinical episodes, revealing elevated LFP power in the theta to low gamma frequencies during choreic storms compared to baseline event recordings. Episode-associated increases in LFP power captured during choreic storms may represent a putative within-patient electrophysiological correlate of these severe episodic exacerbations. Although requiring confirmation and extension in larger series, these observations suggest that adaptive stimulation paradigms could be useful for patients experiencing choreic storms.

title: Temporal organization of leptin signaling reveals distinct regulatory roles for STAT3 and ETV6.
abstract: Leptin regulates energy homeostasis through activation of its long-form receptor (LepRb), primarily via JAK2-dependent phosphorylation of STAT3. However, the temporal organization of leptin-induced transcriptional responses and how parallel signaling pathways contribute to these dynamics remain incompletely understood. Here, we established a LepRb-expressing hypothalamic cellular model to investigate the temporal architecture of leptin-induced transcription factors and pathways identified by transcriptome and proteome profiling at baseline (0 min), early (30 min), and late (180 min) time points. Overall changes in acute leptin stimulation were primarily reflected at the level of transcriptional and regulatory reprogramming. Proteomic remodeling mirrored the transcriptome but appeared smaller, likely due to assay insensitivity and slower dynamics of protein regulation, making the transcriptome the more informative kinetic readout. Structured transcriptional dynamics included the rapid activation of stress- and inflammatory-associated genes followed by sustained cytokine and interferon signaling modules. Transcription factor regulon and pathway activity inference identified coordinated activation of STAT, NF-κB, and MAPK-associated regulatory programs underlying these expression trajectories. CRISPR-Cas9-based deletion of Stat3 markedly altered basal transcriptional states and attenuated leptin-induced gene expression while revealing activation of alternative signaling pathways. In contrast, CRISPR-Cas9-based deletion of the ETS transcriptional repressor Etv6 strongly affected baseline transcription but had minimal impact on leptin-induced regulatory dynamics. Together, these findings reveal a temporally organized regulatory architecture in which STAT3 governs stimulus-responsive transcriptional dynamics, whereas ETV6 primarily modulates baseline transcriptional states.

title: [TH-positive neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla mediating electroacupuncture to improve intestinal motility dysfunction in functional constipated mice].
journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
abstract: To investigate the role of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) in the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on intestinal dysmotility in mice with functional constipation (FC). Firstly, transsynaptic tracing virus was employed to identify brain regions projecting to the proximal colon. Secondly, eighteen C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the normal, model, and EA groups, with 6 mice in each group. FC model was established by oral administration of loperamide hydrochloride. Mice in the EA group received EA at "Tianshu" (ST25) and "Shangjuxu" (ST37), 5 days per treatment course for 2 courses. After intervention, the defecation status of mice in each group was observed, and the fecal water content was determined, the time for the first black stool excretion was recorded, the small-intestinal propulsion rate was measured. Serum and colonic TH levels were determined by ELISA. TH/c-Fos co-expression in the RVLM was assessed by immunofluorescence staining. Subsequently, 12 C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into the control virus+clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) group and inhibitory-virus+CNO group, with 6 mice per group. Another 18 C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the control virus+CNO group, EA group, and excitatory-virus+CNO+EA group, with 6 mice per group. The corresponding viral vectors were injected into the RVLM, followed by intraperitoneal administration of CNO (1 mg/kg) 21 d after viral expression. Mice in the EA and excitatory-virus+CNO+EA groups received EA treatment as described above 30 min after the administration of CNO. Following completion of EA treatment, fecal parameters and intestinal motility were assessed as described above. Finally, rAAV-hSyn-GCaMP6s virus was injected into the RVLM of another 18 C57BL/6J mice. After 21 days of viral transduction, mice were randomly assigned to normal control, model control, and model+EA groups (6 mice per group). Mice in the model+EA group received EA treatment as described above. Post-EA intervention, multichannel fiber photometry was employed to record calcium signal dynamics in RVLM neurons. Neuronal fibers in the RVLM formed synaptic connections with the proximal colon. Compared with the normal group, the model group exhibited prolonged first black stool expulsion time, reduced total fecal pellet counts, decreased fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01), and elevated TH levels in serum and colon (P<0.01). TH and c-Fos, as well as TH/c-Fos co-expression positive cell counts in the RVLM, were all significantly increased (P<0.001). Compared with the model group, the EA group showed shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01), and reduced TH levels in serum and colon (P<0.01). TH and c-Fos expression, as well as TH/c-Fos positive cell counts in the RVLM, were all significantly decreased (P<0.001). Compared with the control virus+CNO group, the inhibitory-virus+CNO group exhibited shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, and elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the control virus+CNO group, the EA group showed shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the EA group, the excitatory-virus+CNO+EA group showed prolonged first black stool expulsion time, reduced total fecal pellet counts, and decreased fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the normal control group, the model control group exhibited significantly increased Ca2+ activity in the RVLM (P<0.001), whereas EA significantly reduced RVLM Ca2+ activity compared with the model control group (P<0.001). EA at ST25 and ST37 may improve intestinal dysmotility in FC mice by suppressing the activity of TH-positive neurons in the RVLM.

title: [The body-brain mechanism of acupuncture: insight and inspiration from neuroimmunology and regulation of organ function].
journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
abstract: Acupuncture, as a typical representative of non-drug therapy, regulates central functions by activating the peripheral nervous system, and has become a leading hotspot in the field of neuromodulation. Focusing on the body-brain mechanism of acupuncture effects, this article systematically reviews the cutting-edge interdisciplinary advancements in acupuncture research and modern life sciences from 3 dimensions: neuro-immune anti-inflammatory actions, target organ function regulation, and "one acupoint affecting multiple organs" intervention for comorbidities. To analyze the key issues, clarify academic viewpoints, and trigger inspirations and discussions, the following are the main points: 1) Based on the established understanding that acupuncture stimulation activates autonomic nerve pathways such as the brainstem vagus-adrenal and spinal cord sympathetic-splenic axes, to exert anti-inflammatory effects, it has also been revealed that some vagus nerves can directly traverse and form synaptic connections with catecholaminergic neurons in the celiac ganglion via collateral branches, rather than relay on postsynaptic neurons. It further seeks to clarify the hierarchical relationship among the catecholamine anti-inflammatory, cholinergic anti-inflammatory, sympathetic/parasympathetic nerve pathways, particularly paying attention to the relationship between the concentration-dependent receptor affinity of norepinephrine in the inflammatory microenvironment and its association with acupuncture effects. 2) Current researches have demonstrated that acupuncture regulates the homeostasis of the body and internal organs by rebalancing the sympathetic-parasympathetic system at multiple levels, identifying the "off-target" phenomenon caused by the loss of response of tissue cells and receptors under pathological conditions is a key factor affecting the "last mile" of the acupuncture effect. 3) Taking the convergence of different visceral input signaling mediated by the intrinsic structures of the spinal cord, as well as the occurrence of comorbidity in the interactive sensitization of the pelvic and sacral organs as an example, results of modern research have provided possible explanations for the cross-segment's and same-segment's "one acupoint affecting multiple organs" and "multiple acupoints affecting one organ" effects of acupuncture. In summary, this article aims to clarify how acupuncture regulates the body's homeostasis through different body-brain autonomic nervous pathways and levels, and offers a review of existing research through 4 dimensions of thinking and inspiration to stimulate new insights and foster exchange of opinions.

title: Identification of TREK channels in mouse intracardiac ganglion neurons.
abstract: The intracardiac nervous system is a complex neural network formed by a diffuse plexus, the so-called intracardiac ganglion (ICG). These ganglia locally innervate and control heart function, but little is known about how ICG neuronal activity is regulated. Although various ionic currents have been characterized in cardiac tissue, the expression and role of TWIK-related K+ (TREK) channels in ICG neurons remain unexplored. TREK channels, members of the two-pore domain potassium channel family, are essential regulators of neuronal membrane resting potential and excitability, with recognized neuroprotective functions. In this study, we have characterized different ionic currents present in mouse ICG neurons, including tetrodotoxin-sensitive Na+ currents, delayed K+ rectifiers, Ca+2-dependent K+ currents and A, H and M currents. Notably, we provide the first evidence of functional TREK channel expression in these neurons. Our findings suggest that TREK channels contribute to excitability control and cellular homoeostasis in ICG neurons, highlighting their potential relevance to cardiac physiology and disease. KEY POINTS: This study provides the first evidence of functional TWIK-related K+ (TREK) channel expression in intracardiac ganglion (ICG) neurons. Comprehensive profiling of ionic currents shaping excitability in ICG neurons. Neuroprotective TREK channels might emerge as potential therapeutic targets for cardiac disorders.

title: Two New 7/7/6/5-Tetracyclic C25 Steroids From the Marine-Derived Fungus Lodderomyces sp. Z-1.
abstract: Lodderomyces is recognized as a yeast genus with important applications in both food fermentation and medical research. In the present study, two new C25 steroids with a 7/7/6/5-tetracyclic scaffold, named (11R,20R)-11-hydroxy-24-oxocyclocitrinol (1) and (11R)-11-hydroxy-erythro-23-O-methylneocyclocitrinol D (2), together with nine known analogues (3-11), were isolated and characterized from the marine-derived fungus Lodderomyces sp. Z-1, which was obtained from the starfish Culcita novaeguineae collected from the South China Sea. The structures and absolute configurations of new compounds were established through extensive spectroscopic analyses, quantum chemical calculations, and comparison of spectral data with those of related analogues reported in the literature. Additionally, the single-crystal x-ray crystallographic structure of the known compound 4 is reported here for the first time. In the anti-inflammatory assay, compound 10 exhibited weak inhibitory activity against LPS-induced NO production in RAW264.7 macrophages with an IC50 value of 41.72 ± 1.81 µM.

title: Design, Synthesis of 3-n-Butylphthalide-Hydrazine/Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Ischemic Stroke Agents.
abstract: To identify novel therapeutic candidates for ischemic stroke, a series of hydrazine- and hydrazide-derived analogs based on 3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) were designed and synthesized in this study, and their anti-ischemic stroke activities were systematically assessed. Among all synthesized derivatives, the compound NBP-HY exerted potent antiplatelet aggregation and antioxidant activities in vitro. Consistent in vivo results revealed that NBP-HY significantly alleviated thrombus formation in both carrageenan-induced tail thrombosis and FeCl3-induced carotid artery thrombosis models. In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) injury model, NBP-HY markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, improved cerebral blood perfusion, and protected hippocampal CA1 and cortical neurons, exhibiting superior therapeutic efficacy compared with the lead compound NBP. Further pharmacological experiments showed that NBP-HY exhibits moderate metabolic stability in liver microsomes, good blood-brain barrier permeability in the PAMPA-BBB model, and minimal impact on mice's physiological hemostatic function. Collectively, this work indicates that NBP‑HY has potential as a therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke and warrants further in‑depth investigation.

title: Development and Validation of the 9-item Parkinson's Disease Screening Questionnaire.
abstract: We aimed to develop and validate a brief, self-administered questionnaire integrating motor and prodromal non-motor symptoms for screening Parkinson's disease (PD). We conducted a three-phase study. Phase 1 used a prospectively registered systematic review of 107 studies to generate a 52-item draft. In Phase 2, the draft was refined in 205 participants (122 with early PD and 83 healthy controls) using item-level areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) and age- and sex-adjusted multivariable logistic regression. Phase 3 validated the 9-item Korean PD Screening Questionnaire (KPDSQ) in an independent cohort (n = 246; 122 PD, 45 essential tremor [ET], and 79 controls), and included a 4-week test-retest reassessment. The final 9-item KPDSQ comprises seven motor items (rest tremor, shuffling or short-step gait, slow daily activities, decreased arm swing, soft voice, masked face, and freezing of gait) and two non-motor items (hyposmia and dream-enactment behavior). At a cutoff of ≥2, sensitivity was 88.5% and specificity was 92.4% for distinguishing PD from controls (AUC = 0.970; 95% CI, 0.946-0.984; p < 0.001). At ≥3, the KPDSQ distinguished PD from ET (AUC = 0.774; 95% CI, 0.680-0.847; p < 0.001). Internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.800), test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.921), and scores correlated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores in patients with PD (Spearman's ρ = 0.330; p < 0.001). The 9-item KPDSQ is a reliable, clinically valid screening tool combining motor and prodromal non-motor features. Prospective community-based validation is warranted.

title: Frailty patterns in European surgical patients: The FRAGILE multicentre prospective cohort.
abstract: Frailty represents a multidimensional decline in physiological reserve that increases vulnerability to surgical stress. Its perioperative dynamics and association with outcomes across diverse surgical populations remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to describe the prevalence of frailty before and after surgery and to evaluate its association with postoperative complications, mortality, and hospital length of stay. We conducted a prospective, multicentre European cohort study including adults undergoing elective or emergency surgery under general or regional anaesthesia across 64 participating centres in 10 countries. Each centre contributed data from one to three predefined recruitment days between April 2021 and December 2022. Frailty was assessed preoperatively and at 30 days using the Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), the FRAIL questionnaire, and the Barthel Index. The primary outcome was the association between preoperative frailty and 30-day postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ II); secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, postoperative cognitive impairment, and new-onset frailty. Among 1472 patients (mean age 60.9 years; 52.9% male), preoperative frailty prevalence was 14.6% (FRAIL), 10.4% (CFS), and 10.4% (Barthel). Within 30 days, 11.9% of nonfrail patients became frail, increasing overall frailty prevalence to 21.2%. Postoperative complications occurred in 19.2% and mortality in 1.7%. Preoperative frailty was independently associated with complications: adjusted odds ratio (OR) 2.35 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.53 to 3.60], P < 0.001); 30-day mortality OR 10.9 (95% CI 1.28 to 93.0), P = 0.029). Frailty was also associated with postoperative cognitive impairment: OR 3.47 (95% CI 1.98 to 6.08), P < 0.001). Frailty is common among surgical patients, increases after surgery, and independently predicts postoperative complications and mortality. These findings highlight frailty as a dynamic and potentially modifiable marker of surgical vulnerability that should be routinely assessed and integrated into perioperative care. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04140370.

title: Interferon-γ Mitigates Oxaliplatin-Induced Neurotoxicity: Analogies With Connexin 43.
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced neuropathy is a major side effect of platinum-based drugs such as oxaliplatin. Given the context-dependent pro-inflammatory or neuroprotective actions of interferon-γ (IFN-γ), this study investigated its role in an in vitro model of oxaliplatin-induced neurotoxicity (OIPN). Rat organotypic spinal cord slices were exposed to oxaliplatin to model chemotherapy-induced neurotoxicity responses in vitro. IFN-γ cytotoxicity was assessed at 6 and 24 h. Neurotoxicity, inflammatory mediators, neurotrophic factors, and markers of glial and neuronal activation were analyzed by biochemical and immunohistochemical assays. Connexin 43 (Cx43) was assessed using Gap19 and Gap27 to probe hemichannel and gap-junction contributions. Electrophysiological recordings characterized neuronal excitability. IFN-γ (6.5-200 ng/mL) was non-toxic and, at 65 ng/mL, significantly reduced oxaliplatin-induced neurotoxicity, decreasing LDH release and suppressing pro-inflammatory mediators (CCL2, SerpinA3N, CGRP, substance P, c-Fos). IFN-γ modulated its signaling by reducing IFNγR and increasing IRF1 expression. It prevented oxaliplatin-induced overexpression of neurotrophic factors and reduced glial and neuronal hyperactivation markers, preserving neuronal integrity. IFN-γ reduced Cx43 expression and hemichannel activity, and Gap19 reproduced selected protective effects. Electrophysiology showed attenuation of oxaliplatin-induced neuronal hyperexcitability. IFN-γ attenuates oxaliplatin-induced neurotoxic responses in an in vitro spinal cord model. The parallel reduction in Cx43 expression and hemichannel activity supports further investigation of Cx43 signaling as a candidate pharmacological target in OIPN.

title: Multimodal Brain Graph Analysis for Uncovering Path-Based Biomarkers in Schizophrenia: Integrating Static and Dynamic Approaches.
abstract: Analyzing multimodal brain networks offers new insights into the mechanisms of brain disorders. However, most studies focus on unimodal networks or use global/local graph metrics, often missing critical information about disrupted pathways. In this study, we propose a novel framework for estimating static and dynamic multimodal brain graphs by integrating time-resolved functional network connectivity (FNC) and gray matter features using a Gaussian graphical model. We then apply a path-based graph theory analysis to identify connectors and disconnectors, edges that respectively introduce or eliminate paths in the patient graph compared to controls. Our findings in schizophrenia reveal several edges linked to missing or additional paths, indicating network disruptions that are undetectable using unimodal or pairwise analyses. These disrupted pathways span both within- and cross-modal connections, particularly involving regions like the middle temporal gyrus and cerebellum. This work demonstrates the value of multimodal integration and emphasizes the importance of moving beyond individual edge-level analysis when characterizing disease-related network alterations. Our path-centric approach provides a complementary view of brain connectivity disruption and identifies candidate path-based markers of schizophrenia that warrant validation in independent datasets.

title: Major Depressive Disorder With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury in Adolescents: Altered Morphological Inverse Divergence Gradient in Brain Structure and Gene Expression Patterns.
abstract: Adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD) and non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) face serious challenges to their mental and physical health. The development of this condition is influenced by genetic, environmental, and brain development factors. In this study, we used the Morphometric Inverse Divergence Gradient Network (MIND-Gd) for the first time to explore brain structural network abnormalities and their transcriptional mechanisms in adolescents with MDD and NSSI. A total of 241 adolescents with MDD participated in this study. Among them, 134 had NSSI, while 107 did not. Using high-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), we constructed the principal MIND gradient network. This network reflects the similarity of cortical morphology between different brain regions. The results showed that adolescents with NSSI had higher MIND gradient values in the left caudal middle frontal gyrus and bilateral inferior temporal gyri. In contrast, lower values were observed in the left lingual gyrus and right superior parietal lobule. These structural changes were spatially correlated with functional alterations in the dorsal attention network. Further analysis revealed that these differences were linked to the distribution of nine types of neurotransmitter receptors, including 5-HT1A, GABAa, glutamate, and dopamine. Partial least squares regression analysis (PLS) was also conducted. The first component (PLS1) explained 39.53% of the spatial variance in MIND-Gd. This analysis identified key genes related to NSSI, such as GABRA5 and MGST1. Enrichment analysis showed that PLS1+ genes were involved in synaptic signaling, neurodevelopment, and mood disorder pathways. These genes were enriched in astrocytes and cortical layers I, II, and V. On the other hand, PLS1- genes were linked to chromatin regulation and cytoskeletal metabolism. These genes were mainly expressed in Cortical Layers III and IV. In conclusion, adolescents with MDD and NSSI show specific abnormalities in brain structural gradients. These abnormalities are closely related to neurotransmitter receptor distributions and gene expression patterns. The findings provide multi-level evidence for understanding the neurobiological mechanisms of NSSI.

title: Disease-specific body composition patterns in children with cerebral palsy and spinal muscular atrophy.
journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cerebral palsy (CP) are severe neurological conditions characterized by neurodegeneration and non-progressive brain injury, respectively, both profoundly affecting the nutritional status in children. This observational study aimed to comprehensively assess and compare anthropometry and body composition across groups of children with SMA, CP, and healthy controls (HCs). We enrolled three age- and sex-matched groups of 40 children each: CP (Gross Motor Function Classification System IV-V), SMA (Types I-II), and HC. Anthropometry, skinfolds, and circumferences were collected, and relative z-score was calculated. Body fat percentage (BF%) was estimated using the Slaughter equation; fat mass index (FMI), fat-free mass (FFM), and FFM Index (FFMI) were calculated. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and robust linear regression were performed adjusting for sex, age, body mass index z-score (BMIz), epilepsy, feeding via, ventilation, and pharmacological treatment. BMIz was significantly lower in children with neurological impairment than in HC, with no difference between CP and SMA (HC: 0.04 [-0.5; 0.6]; CP: -1.8 [-4.3; -0.6]; SMA: -3.0 [-4.7; -1.2], p < 0.0001). After adjustments, SMA group showed 17.02% higher BF% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 8.27-25.78; p = 0.0003) and higher FMI (+1.37; 95% CI: 0.98-3.75; p = 0.001), compared to CP. When referenced to HC, FMI was higher in SMA and lower in CP. Lastly, SMA showed lower FFMI compared to both CP and HC. SMA is characterized by higher BF% and a marked deficit in FFM compared to CP, independently of BMIz, epilepsy, feeding via, and pharmacological treatment. Neurological impairments are associated with distinct body composition patterns, highlighting the need for personalized nutritional assessment.

title: Charting Cervical Spinal Cord Morphometry Across the Lifespan.
abstract: Spinal cord morphometry provides essential biomarkers of neurological health, but clinical interpretations are confounded by inter-subject variability and a lack of normative references across the full human lifespan. We address this gap by generating the first comprehensive lifespan charts for cervical spinal cord morphometry. From 78,269 T1-weighted brain MRI sessions, we identified a final cross-sectional cohort of 24,251 healthy or cognitively normal controls from 33 datasets (ages 0-100 years) with cervical cord coverage. To overcome contrast variability, we employed a state-of-the-art contrast-agnostic deep learning segmentation method, extracting cross-sectional area (CSA), anteroposterior (AP) and right-left (RL/transverse), and shape indices (AP/RL ratio, eccentricity, and solidity) from C1 to C7. Normative trajectories were modeled using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS). The resulting charts reveal distinct non-linear lifespan changes: rapid growth through childhood and adolescence, peak maturation occurring in early-to-mid adulthood (e.g., mid-30s for CSA), followed by gradual decreases. Significant regional variations along the cervical cord and consistent sex differences (males > females for size metrics) were quantified. Spinal cord trajectories showed strong temporal coupling with brain white matter and brainstem volumes, suggesting integrated CNS development and aging. These lifespan charts provide a robust normative framework, enabling age- and sex-specific centile scoring of individual spinal cord morphometry. This resource offers a critical tool for differentiating typical variation from pathological changes, enhancing the clinical utility of spinal cord MRI in studies of development and neurodegeneration.
