title: EXPRESS: How error rates scale with chance rate among dogs following human pointing gestures, and why it matters.
abstract: Humans use pointing gestures to communicate with dogs. However, efforts to study how dogs receive this communicative signal have produced ambiguous results. Prior work presenting a choice between two options has shown that dogs choose the pointed-to option at above chance levels, but just barely. With only two options, the high probability of choosing correctly by chance weakens the signal. After replicating the 2-option task, we changed the task's parameters by presenting dogs with six options. We compared two models that make divergent, quantitative predictions on how the success rates will relate on the two tasks. One model stresses that multiplying the options should reduce the number of correct choices made by chance at a higher rate than instances of genuine communication. A second model that involves no understanding of referents, but just a systematic shift in attention, predicts the effect size to remain constant irrespective of the number of options. Dogs chose the location pointed to at barely above chance rates in both the 2-choice and 6-choice tasks. This pattern discourages the view that dogs understand the referential aspect of human pointing. Additional patterns that become visible with more than two options bolster this interpretation. Dogs chose the correct side of the arena and succeeded on second choices disproportionately more often. Dogs succeeded with far and near locations at similar rates. These results challenge the view that dogs interpret human pointing as referring to a specific object, which has implications for claims that point-following evinces intentional capacities among dogs.

title: Comparing the coherent point drift algorithm to sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic whole-bone three-dimensional shape analyses.
abstract: The ability to quantify 3D morphologies is critical for anatomical research; however, setting up high-density landmark sets and positioning them on all specimens can represent a substantial challenge. The coherent point drift (CPD) algorithm, a technique for registering two point clouds based on the Gaussian mixture model, was recently used to investigate human variation; however, its performance has yet to be compared to other 3D shape analysis methods. Here we compare the results of a CPD analysis to a sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic (SPHARM) analysis of the same 60 human and African ape calcanei and a CPD analysis and SPHARM-sliding analysis (a combination SPHARM and sliding semilandmark analysis) of 40 primate third manual proximal phalanges (mPP3s) to determine methodological comparability. Additionally, we run a CPD analysis on a small but wide-ranging sample of primate ulnae to demonstrate its utility for proximodistally long and mediolaterally narrow long bones. All specimens were surface or micro-CT scanned. All calcanei were subjected to a CPD analysis with 2000 semilandmarks, a sliding semilandmark analysis with 1007 semilandmarks, and a SPHARM analysis. All mPP3s underwent a CPD analysis with 2500 semilandmarks and a SPHARM-sliding analysis with 2562 semilandmarks. For the ulna, a CPD analysis with 1252 semilandmarks was run. Shape variation for all analyses was summarized using (separate) principal component analyses (PCAs). Results of the respective analyses for the calcaneus and mPP3 were compared by calculating the maximum and root mean square distances (RMSD) between average taxon shape configurations (scaled based on centroid size) generated from each analysis. All three calcaneus analyses separate taxa along the first two PCs, with humans separating from African apes along PC1 and chimpanzees and gorillas separating across PC2. For the two mPP3 analyses, the three great ape taxa consistently separate along PC1, and Papio separates from the other taxa along PC2. The average RMSD between CPD and sliding semilandmark analyses for the calcaneus was 0.24 mm, and 0.21 mm between CPD and SPHARM analyses. For the mPP3, the average RMSD between CPD and SPHARM-sliding was 0.14 mm. These results indicate that CPD is a comparable 3D shape analysis method to these other approaches. The CPD analysis was also able to place a semilandmark set on primate ulnae ranging from gorillas to tarsiers and capture morphological variations including shaft curvature, relative olecranon process length, and overall robusticity. CPD analyses are less time intensive than sliding semilandmark analyses; however, the sliding semilandmark analysis was better able to capture variation surrounding the borders of the articular facets (although differences were relatively minor), suggesting that these analyses may be better suited when the researcher is interested in a specific anatomical feature. CPD did capture edges better than SPHARM analyses; however, this is likely not an issue for small, relatively round bones such as carpals and most tarsals. In sum, CPD produces similar results to sliding semilandmark, SPHARM, and SPHARM-sliding approaches and has benefits for analyses of long bones with complex morphologies or among taxa that exhibit large amounts of morphological variation.

title: MRI-Derived Muscle Fat Fraction Reflects Disease Severity and Functional Impairment in Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 1A.
abstract: Progressive intramuscular fat infiltration is a hallmark of neuromuscular degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A). Quantitative assessment of muscle fat fraction (FF) by Dixon magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides an objective biomarker of disease severity, but manual segmentation is laborious and variable. This study explored whether automated MRI-based FF quantification reflects disease severity and functional decline in CMT1A. Sixty-nine genetically confirmed patients with CMT1A who underwent 3D multi-echo Dixon lower-leg MRI were retrospectively analyzed. A deep learning-based segmentation model delineated four muscle compartments (anterior, lateral, deep posterior, superficial posterior) and mean FFs were computed volumetrically. Correlations were tested between MRI-derived FFs and clinical outcomes, including the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Score (CMTNSv2), Functional Disability Scale (FDS), and time-, strength-, distance-, and repetition-based performance. Partial correlations were adjusted for age and body mass index. All compartmental and total FFs correlated positively with CMTNSv2 and FDS (r = 0.39-0.49, p < 0.05). FFs were positively associated with time-based and negatively with strength-, distance-, and repetition-based measures. FF Anterior showed moderate correlations with stair climb time (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and 6-min walk distance (r = -0.66, p < 0.001), with similar magnitudes across compartments. Most associations remained significant after adjustment. The lateral compartment showed the highest FF (median 33.2%), consistent with the peroneal pattern of CMT1A. Automated MRI-based FF quantification provides a reproducible biomarker of disease burden in CMT1A, reflecting clinical severity and functional decline, and may serve as an imaging outcome measure in future studies.

title: Acute caffeine and carbohydrate strategies for fatigue-related sport-specific performance in team-sport athletes: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Although caffeine and carbohydrate are established ergogenic strategies for physical performance, it remains unclear whether these benefits translate to the decision-making and sport-specific skills that determine team-sport performance under fatigue. PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and SPORTDiscus were searched on 28 July 2026. Thirty-one reports were retained; their reported analyzed sample sizes summed to 441 athletes. Twenty-three independent quantitative study clusters, with reported analyzed sample sizes summing to 341 athletes, contributed 67 effects. Multilevel random-effects models nested effect sizes within studies; primary assumptions were r = 0.5 and rho = 0.80. Inference used CR2 robust standard errors and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Soccer supplied 11 of the 23 quantitative clusters; every other sport category supplied four or fewer. Broad caffeine was centered near zero (Hedges' g = 0.040, 95% CI -0.211 to 0.291; p = 0.691; df = 4.41). Tier 1a perceptual-motor and Tier 1b technical/tactical estimates were imprecise. Broad carbohydrate was positive but uncertain (g = 0.256, 95% CI -0.094 to 0.605; p = 0.118; df = 4.96), and one study cluster materially influenced this estimate. All six GRADE comparisons were rated very low certainty. The two-study mental-fatigue calculation was too fragile for conventional inference. Current evidence does not support assuming that the established physical ergogenic effects of caffeine translate to fatigue-related decision-making or sport-specific skill. Carbohydrate may provide a small benefit, but the evidence remains sparse and highly uncertain. Sensitivity to study composition was driven primarily by one influential cluster, whose omission increased the pooled estimate. The carbohydrate estimates apply only to heterogeneous ingested-beverage protocols and should not be extrapolated to mouth-rinse or gel strategies. Parallel syntheses do not establish intervention superiority or combined-strategy synergy.

title: Intention-to-Leave Among New Zealand Podiatrists: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Frequency and Associated Factors.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research
abstract: Workforce retention poses ongoing challenges for podiatric care provision in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ); however, intention-to-leave (ITL) from the workforce and its associated factors have not been explored. This study aimed to determine the frequency of ITL among NZ podiatrists and identify factors associated with leaving intentions. A cross-sectional online survey of NZ-registered practising podiatrists was conducted. Demographics, employment, workplace and attitudinal measures were collected as independent variables. ITL was assessed using (1) a self-reported single-item Likert scale and (2) total scores on the validated six-item Turnover Intention Scale (TIS-6), with higher scores indicating greater turnover intention. Associations between both ITL outcomes and independent variables were examined using theory-informed hierarchical logistic and linear regression models, as appropriate. A total of 143 podiatrist responses were analysed. Over half (50.7%) reported being somewhat or highly likely to leave the profession, with 23.8% indicating plans to exit within 2 years. The mean TIS-6 total score was 15.41/30 (SD 5.16). In fully adjusted models, workplace and psychosocial factors demonstrated the most consistent associations with ITL. Lower organisational support (OR = 0.60, p = 0.049), lower role satisfaction (OR 0.64, p = 0.041; B = -2.08, p ≤ 0.001), lower perceived professional respect (B = -1.14, p < 0.05) and higher stress levels (OR 0.57, p = 0.023) were associated with greater ITL. ITL among NZ podiatrists is prevalent, with over half of this sample reporting some ITL and almost one quarter considering a near-term exit. Given the relatively small NZ podiatry workforce, these findings raise important concerns regarding future workforce sustainability and service-provision capacity. Addressing modifiable factors such as role satisfaction, organisational support, professional value and workplace stress may represent important targets for retention initiatives.

title: Viral Infection-Induced Epilepsy and the Gut Microbiome Crosstalk.
abstract: Viral infections of the central nervous system (CNS) pose a significant risk for seizures, and in some cases, long-term epileptogenesis. Seizure development following viral infection involves diverse CNS mechanisms, with emerging evidence that peripheral factors, including gut microbiome composition and immune-inflammatory responses, also contribute. The gut microbiome is a multifaceted ecosystem with important roles in CNS health, and advances in sequencing have enabled investigation of host and microbial genomic changes associated with seizure development. While both animal and human studies link gut dysbiosis to epilepsy, including infection-induced epilepsy, the specific effects of viral-induced seizures on the gut microbiome remain unclear. Moreover, the influence of virus-triggered epileptogenesis is not well understood. This review summarizes current knowledge on viral infections linked to seizures and highlights the limited but growing evidence for gut microbial changes in this context. We focus on Zika virus (ZIKV), West Nile virus (WNV), and herpes simplex virus-1 (HSV-1), all implicated in human epileptogenesis, though direct microbiome-seizure connections are still limited. We also discuss severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2), which causes neurological symptoms without consistently inducing seizures in rodent models despite neurological involvement, and Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV), a murine virus widely used as a model of infection-induced seizures because it induces strain-dependent seizures in mice. Current evidence suggests associations among viral infections, gut microbiome alterations, and seizure occurrence; however, further causative studies are needed to define their roles and elucidate underlying mechanisms.

title: Third Trimester-Equivalent Alcohol Exposure Induces Alterations in Locomotor Activity, Anxiety and Risk-Related Behaviors, and Susceptibility to Mechanical Allodynia in Adulthood in Mice.
abstract: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) can lead to the development of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASDs), which are neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by behavioral dysregulation, learning deficits, and cognitive inflexibilities. Alcohol exposure is harmful at all stages of human gestation, including the third trimester. This developmental window-characterized by rapid brain growth, myelination, and neural circuit formation-may be particularly vulnerable, yet the long-lasting behavioral and sensory consequences of exposure during this period remain poorly understood. In this study, neonatal mouse pups were exposed to Air or ethanol (EtOH) vapor from postnatal day (P) 4 to P8, which is equivalent to a third trimester alcohol exposure (TTAE) in humans. Blood ethanol concentrations measured at P8 reached approximately 250 mg/dL, consistent with binge-level exposure. Air- and EtOH-exposed mice were then assessed as adults at 5-6 months of age for spontaneous locomotor activity and gait control, exploratory and anxiety-related behavior, recognition memory and novelty preference, and susceptibility to neuropathic pain following minor chronic constriction injury (mCCI) of the sciatic nerve. TTAE produced long-lasting behavioral outcomes in adulthood, several of which differed between males and females. EtOH-exposed males exhibited increased spontaneous locomotor activity in a single-housed cage and increased open-arm exploration in the Elevated Zero Maze, with significant Sex × Treatment interactions for both measures. In the Novel Object Recognition task, EtOH-exposed males exhibited a strong preference for the familiar rather than the novel object. EtOH-exposed males also exhibited stronger alterations in gait parameters than EtOH-exposed females. Following mCCI, both EtOH-exposed male and female mice developed persistent mechanical allodynia that was largely absent in Air-exposed controls. These findings demonstrate that TTAE may permanently disrupt behavioral regulation and increase susceptibility to neuropathic pain in adulthood. The differential responses between males and females indicate that some long-term behavioral consequences of TTAE are sex-dependent.

title: Acetaminophen-induced liver injury triggers short- and long-term neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and behavioral deficits in a genetic mouse model of autism.
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition with a strong genetic basis, yet its etiology is not fully understood. Neuroinflammation is emerging as a critical secondary factor. Since peripheral organ injury, such as acute liver failure, can induce neuroinflammation, we aimed to investigate whether liver injury could exacerbate ASD-like phenotypes in a genetically susceptible model. We used adult (12-month-old) Shank3-/- mice, a genetic model of ASD, and their wild-type (WT) counterparts. A single high dose of acetaminophen (APAP; 350 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally to induce acute liver injury. We assessed acute (24-h) and long-term (1-month) consequences on liver health, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier integrity, and brain edema using plasma biomarkers, immunohistochemistry, and in-vivo MRI, as well as behavioral phenotypes, including sociability, repetitive behaviors and exploration. Acutely, APAP induced severe liver damage, cerebral edema, and neuroinflammation in Shank3-/- mice. One month later, despite liver recovery, both APAP-treated WT and Shank3-/- mice exhibited brain edema, elevated apparent transverse relaxation (R2*) rates, and lasting neuroinflammation, evidenced by microgliosis and reactive astrocytosis. These differences were more extensive in the Shank3-/- group. Behaviorally, this was accompanied by increased social deficits in both genotypes. Critically, only the APAP-treated Shank3-/- mice displayed significantly increased repetitive behaviors, and reduced exploratory activity. Here, we show that transient liver injury is associated with long-term neuroinflammation, markers of blood-brain barrier disruption, and behavioral deficits. These findings demonstrate that while peripheral organ damage can induce lasting behavioral changes in healthy animals, the severity and spectrum of these deficits are exacerbated by ASD-associated genetic predisposition. These findings support a preclinical gene-environment interaction framework relevant to ASD-associated vulnerability.

title: Effects of local vibration therapy and gabapentin on restless legs syndrome symptoms: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of LV in combination with gabapentin, a first-line medication for RLS, on the treatment of patients with the condition. In total, 36 participants (18 in each group) participated in this study, with 10 (55%) being male within each group. The mean age of participants was 45 years (SD = 10.6) in the LV group and 49.1 (SD = 8.3) in the gabapentin group. In both the LV and gabapentin groups, IRLSSG scores decreased significantly after the intervention compared with baseline (p 0.05). The study protocol was registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials on August 30th, 2023 (code IRCT20190306042945N4).

title: Initiating levodopa pump therapy: a qualitative study of patient and caregiver perspectives.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting motor and non-motor functions. When oral medication no longer provides adequate control, device-aided therapies (DAT), including levodopa infusion therapy, may be introduced. Although DAT can improve symptom management, little is known about how people with PD (PwPD) and family caregivers (FC) experience the initiation process. This study explored PwPD and their FC perceptions during decision-making, therapy initiation, and subsequent adaptation to levodopa pump therapy. This qualitative study employed semi-structured interviews (6-24 months after treatment initiation) and latent reflexive thematic analysis with ten PwPD and nine FC recruited from two Swedish university hospitals. Thematic analysis revealed four shared themes: (1) Living with the constraints of PD, (2) Sustaining hope in the face of therapeutic uncertainty, (3) Adapting to a new treatment while facing practical challenges, and (4) Relying on expertise while managing its absence. Pump therapy was often chosen due to limited alternatives and strong trust in the specialized multidisciplinary PD team. While both groups experienced symptom improvements, PwPD focused on autonomy whereas FC focused on responsibilities. Expectations were generally met, yet FC frequently felt underinformed about the realities of daily pump management. Our findings highlight that although symptom control improved, both PwPD and FC continued to face practical and emotional challenges. Supporting their adaptation process requires coordinated, person-centred preparation, guidance and follow-up from multidisciplinary, specialized PD teams. Not applicable.

title: Functionalized metal-organic frameworks as smart nanoplatforms: advancing tumor precision therapy through post-synthetic surface tailoring, challenges, and prospects for clinical translation.
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have garnered significant attention as versatile nanocarriers for oncological drug delivery, owing to their exceptional porosity, structural tunability, extensive specific surface areas, and favorable drug loading and release kinetics, which collectively enable targeted payload delivery and reduced systemic toxicity. Nevertheless, the clinical promise of unmodified MOFs is severely curtailed by substantial in vivo biological barriers-including rapid bio-clearance, the immunosuppressive and acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), and inefficient cellular internalization-challenges that are ubiquitous across nanomedicine platforms and critically undermine therapeutic outcomes. This review provides a comprehensive examination of post-synthetic modification (PSM) as an indispensable strategy to surmount these obstacles. It systematically categorizes the diverse array of surface modifiers reported to date into natural polymers, synthetic polymers, nonpolymeric small molecules, inorganic materials, and multifunctional hybrid architectures, while elucidating how each class can enhance biocompatibility, colloidal stability, circulation half-life, active targeting, and stimuli-responsive cargo release. Crucially, the review critically appraises the intrinsic trade-offs introduced by surface engineering, including increased hydrodynamic diameter, impaired tumor penetration, heightened synthetic and characterization complexity, and unpredictable perturbations to biodegradation pathways and immune system interactions. Despite robust preclinical validation, the translational trajectory of surface-engineered MOF-based therapeutics remains encumbered by formidable challenges spanning scalable and reproducible manufacturing, long-term biosafety assessment, and stringent regulatory approval. By delineating current advances, critical limitations, and prospective directions, this review highlights the delicate equilibrium between surface functionalization and biological performance that must be achieved to realize the clinical potential of PSM-optimized MOF nanomedicines.

title: Association between perinatal intimate partner violence and breastfeeding outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) negatively affects the health of both the mother and the child. These risks are particularly critical during the perinatal period, a time of heightened vulnerability. However, the relationship between maternal IPV exposure and breastfeeding outcomes remains uncertain, and existing findings are inconsistent and inconclusive. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesise the existing evidence on the association between perinatal IPV and breastfeeding outcomes. A systematic literature search was conducted using relevant databases between June 15 and August 2, 2024. All peer-reviewed observational studies that specifically investigated the link between Perinatal (P)-IPV and breastfeeding outcomes, such as early initiation, exclusivity, and duration among the perinatal population, were included. Heterogeneity across the included studies was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I² statistics. Publication bias was assessed through funnel plots and Egger's test. Finally, a random effects model was used to estimate the pooled adjusted odds ratios and their 95% CIs. Nineteen observational studies published between 2007 and 2024, comprising 347,706 mother-child pairs, were included in the review. Of these, 17 studies were eligible for the meta-analysis. A meta-analysis of nine studies indicated that P-IPV was associated with a 36% higher odds of delayed initiation of breastfeeding (AOR: 1.36; 95% CI: 1.14-1.63), with both physical (AOR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.02-1.42) and psychological P-IPV (AOR: 1.38; 95% CI: 1.09-1.74) were associated with higher odds of not initiating breastfeeding within one hour of birth. Similarly, women exposed to P-IPV had higher odds of not exclusively breastfeeding (EBF) at six months (AOR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.21-1.85), with similar associations observed for both physical (AOR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.18-1.95) and psychological P-IPV (AOR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.39-1.76). This review found that P-IPV was associated with delayed breastfeeding initiation and a lower likelihood of EBF at six months. The findings highlight the potential value of trauma-informed and trauma-sensitive screening, support, and referral pathways for women experiencing P-IPV.

title: Cross-species molecular stratification enables T cell receptor diagnosis of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Developing peripheral blood-based diagnostic models for idiopathic Parkinson's disease (iPD), particularly those leveraging the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, has long been considered infeasible because patient-derived TCRs appear to lack convergent sequence motifs. We reasoned that this apparent absence of shared TCR features likely reflects both insufficient sample sizes and unaccounted immune heterogeneity within the iPD population. We reconstructed TCR repertoires from the two largest iPD cohorts currently available, anchoring them with three mechanistically distinct mouse models to stratify patients into model-anchored informed subtypes. Within these data-driven subtypes, we trained subtype-specific, multimodal multi-instance classifiers. We demonstrated that iPD patients can be successfully stratified into model-anchored informed subtypes. Furthermore, the trained subtype-specific, multimodal multi-instance classifiers achieved an Area Under Curve (AUC) exceeding 0.8 for both subtypes. Our findings underscore the critical role of disease stratification in enabling TCR repertoire-based modeling in neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Reduced neural sensitivity to emotional faces and voices in preterm five-year-olds: a comparative study.
abstract: Accurate emotion processing is crucial for social development. Preterm birth is associated with neurodevelopmental alterations and increased vulnerability to subtle socio-emotional difficulties, often described within the preterm behavioral phenotype. Previous studies have reported impaired emotion recognition in preterm populations, but have largely relied on behavioral tasks and primarily focused on facial expressions. Because explicit emotion recognition is still developing in early childhood, objective neural markers of implicit emotion discrimination may be particularly informative for early detection. We administered a series of frequency-tagging electroencephalography (EEG) paradigms to investigate neural sensitivity to brief changes in emotional expressions in a cohort of five-year-old preterm children (N = 66), and age-matched full-term peers (N = 32). Frequency-tagging EEG utilizes fast periodic stimulation to elicit synchronized brain responses measurable in the frequency domain. Neural sensitivity to changes in emotional expressions was examined in both the visual and auditory modality, using oddball paradigms with neutral faces or voices presented at base frequency and emotional expressions (either fearful or happy) presented as periodic oddballs. Linear mixed models were used to investigate the effects of group, emotion, and prematurity severity. All children showed implicit neural discrimination between neutral and emotional expressions. Compared to full-term peers, children born before 32 weeks of gestation, but not those born between 33 and 36 weeks of gestation, showed reduced neural sensitivity to facial emotional expression changes. In contrast, all preterm children (< 37 weeks of gestation) showed reduced neural sensitivity to vocal emotional expression changes. Across modalities, reduced neural sensitivity to happy emotional expressions was associated with higher parent-reported social difficulties. Five-year-old children born preterm show reduced neural sensitivity to brief changes in facial and vocal emotional expressions compared with full-term peers. Strikingly, the impact of prematurity severity differed between the visual and auditory modalities, indicating differential maturation of higher-level visual and auditory processing following preterm birth. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of socio-emotional development after preterm birth and highlight the importance of early, modality-sensitive monitoring of socio-emotional development across the entire preterm population.

title: Cord blood T-Cell imbalances as early predictors of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in extremely preterm neonates.
abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a major morbidity among extremely preterm neonates and has been increasingly linked to dysregulated early-life immune responses. whether cord blood T-cell subset profiles can identify neonates at increased risk of BPD remains unclear. We examined the association between cord blood immune cell subsets and the subsequent BPD and explore immunological measures could improve early risk prediction when combined with clinical variables. In this prospective cohort study, 75 extremely preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation were enrolled at birth. High-parameter flow cytometry was used to quantify innate and adaptive immune cell populations from umbilical cord arterial blood. Clinical data were collected, and BPD was diagnosed at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Multivariable regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression were conducted to identify cord immune features associated with BPD and to develop an exploratory prediction model. Among 75 infants, 31 developed BPD and 44 did not. After adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, duration of mechanical ventilation and amniotic inflammatory syndrome, infants who developed BPD had lower cord blood proportions of CD3⁺ T cells, CD4⁺ T cells, and regulatory T cells, as well as a lower CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T-cell ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression retained pulmonary hemorrhage, regulatory T-cell proportion, duration of oxygen therapy, and intraventricular hemorrhage for the final prediction model. The resulting nomogram showed high apparent discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.959. Decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical utility across a range of threshold probabilities. Extremely preterm infants who developed BPD showed altered cord blood T-cell profiles at birth, particularly reduced regulatory T-cell proportions. A nomogram incorporating regulatory T-cell proportion and selected clinical risk factors may support early identification of infants at increased risk of BPD.

title: Whole-transcriptome sequencing reveals Alzheimer's disease-associated ceRNA regulatory networks and downstream pathways.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) molecular mechanisms remain unclear, and effective therapies are lacking. This study employed whole-transcriptome sequencing to investigate the expression profiles of circRNAs, lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs in the hippocampus of APP/PS1 transgenic mice, aiming to identify ceRNA regulatory networks and clarify their roles in AD pathogenesis. Differentially expressed RNAs were integrated into ceRNA networks, and programmed cell death-related pathways were analyzed using GO and KEGG. The computationally predicted circRNA_13083/miR-298-5p/CD14 axis was preliminarily evaluated in vitro using siRNA-mediated CD14 knockdown in microglial and neuronal AD models. Expression of CD14, NF-κB components, and NLRP3 markers was measured by qRT-PCR, while secreted IL-1β and IL-18 protein levels were quantified via ELISA. Neuronal survival was assessed via CCK-8 assays. Transcriptome analysis revealed 376 differentially expressed mRNAs, 491 lncRNAs, 5,253 circRNAs, and 21 miRNAs, which formed extensive ceRNA interaction networks. Functional enrichment highlighted programmed cell death pathways, including NF-κB and inflammasome signaling. The circRNA_13083/miR-298-5p/CD14 axis emerged as a key regulatory node. qRT-PCR confirmed elevated CD14 expression in AD models. CD14 knockdown significantly attenuated Aβ1-42-induced NF-κB activation, NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, and proinflammatory cytokine release. Conditioned medium transfer experiments further demonstrated that CD14 silencing alleviated microglia-mediated neuronal damage and improved HT-22 cell survival. Whole-transcriptome sequencing uncovered extensive ceRNA regulatory networks in AD hippocampus, with the circRNA_13083/miR-298-5p/CD14 axis potentially implicated in neuroinflammation and programmed cell death through NF-κB signaling. Silencing CD14 mitigates microglial activation and neuronal injury, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for AD.
